title: Copilot Studio: cost visibility in agent evaluations
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, preview credit display, licensing statements and documented controls are supported. The allocation API operation is valid, but its note should identify the request-body properties that set the allocation and tenant-capacity draw.

claims.claim: An agent monthly limit with Stop usage turns the agent off when it reaches the limit.
claims.quote: Turn on Stop usage if the agent should be turned off when it reaches the limit.

claims.claim: With no enabled overage source, an environment can consume only its allocated prepaid credits.
claims.quote: If no overage source is enabled, the environment can consume only its allocated prepaid credits. Experiences that require credits can stop working after that allocation is exhausted.

claims.claim: Agent limits are not applied instantly, and agents can respond for some time after reaching them.
claims.quote: Limits aren't applied instantly. An agent can continue to respond for some time after it reaches its limit, so set limits and notification thresholds with some margin.

claims.claim: Experiences requiring credits can stop working when an environment has none available.
claims.quote: When an environment has no available Copilot Credits, experiences that require credits can stop working.

claims.claim: Credit exhaustion can affect evaluations of Microsoft Copilot harness agents.
claims.quote: Building, testing, evaluating, and running these agents can consume Copilot Credits. ... When an environment has no available Copilot Credits, experiences that require credits can stop working.

claims.claim: Environment tenant-capacity draw is under Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits > environment > Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote: select Licensing. ... Under Products, select Copilot Studio. ... Select Manage Copilot Credits. ... Select the environment. ... Under Capacity overages, clear Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.

claims.claim: PUT /licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 writes an environment allocation and tenant-capacity draw configuration.
claims.quote:
$apiVersion    = "2024-10-01" ... Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put `
    -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion"
claims.fix: Keep the call unchanged. Add to controls[1].note and its rendered table note: 'The request body targets scope.environmentId; allocatedEntitlements uses entitlementId MCSMessages, allocation.quantity and enforcementRules with ruleType TenantPool and enabled false to disable tenant-capacity draw.' These properties are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/programmability-tutorial-manage-copilot-credit-allocations.

claims.claim: Capacity management requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent role able to manage licensing and capacity.
claims.quote: To manage Copilot Studio capacity, you need the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: A published environment-group rule makes the environment's tenant-draw setting read-only.
claims.quote: When you publish a rule, it governs every environment in the group. The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center, and programmatic requests can't override it.

claims.claim: Programmatic updates overriding a published tenant-draw group rule are rejected with TenantPoolLockedByPolicy.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the TenantPoolLockedByPolicy error.

claims.claim: The allocation tutorial uses https://api.powerplatform.com as the API base URL.
claims.quote: $apiBaseUrl    = "https://api.powerplatform.com"

claims.claim: Agent monthly limits are reached through Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Copilot Studio > Manage Agents > agent > Set limit.
claims.quote:
In the Power Platform admin center, go to Licensing > Copilot Studio.
Select Manage Agents.
Select the agent, and then select Set limit.

claims.quote: Changes to shared capacity can affect other Copilot Studio agents, workflows, and features in the same environment.
